html:
Tok Pisin is the English-based creole that is the most widely spoken language of Papua New Guinea, a country with more than 800 languages. Its name comes from talk pidgin.

It grew in the late 19th century among New Guineans who worked on plantations in Samoa and in German New Guinea, and took words from English, German, Malay and Tolai. Missions and the army spread it.

Today most Papua New Guineans speak it, many as their first language, and it is used in parliament, newspapers and churches. It is a close cousin of Bislama in Vanuatu. Its spread helps hold together a country of very many peoples. See also Papuan languages.
